extraction_scope: Worker-6 replaced automated mechanism placeholder notes with source-reviewed mechanism ontology claims anchored to local XML/PDF sections.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Macropin forms an alpha-helical conformation in membrane-mimicking SDS/TFE environments, supporting membrane-active amphipathic behavior but not alone proving killing mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural support only; mechanism assignment relies on additional membrane permeability, depolarization, PI uptake, and SEM evidence.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=7:Structure of the peptide and circular dichroism spectroscopy

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Macropin binds bacterial envelope components: peptidoglycan for S. aureus and LPS for P. aeruginosa.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding evidence supports envelope targeting but is not a standalone bactericidal endpoint.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=9:Binding of Macropin with cell wall components

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Macropin permeabilizes the outer membrane and depolarizes the cytoplasmic membrane in S. aureus and P. aeruginosa assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Macropin against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa
mechanism_claims.limitations: Quantitative curves are figure-based; source text supports the direction and approximate endpoints.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PI flow cytometry and low-vacuum SEM show membrane damage after Macropin treatment.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Macropin-treated S. aureus and P. aeruginosa
mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphology/PI data support membrane damage; they do not define a single pore model.
